The first real marathon race wasn't the distance we run today, and it was won by a man who carried water for a living.
Greece, the United Kingdom or the USA. Three seconds, then the map traces the original route and explains how the race got stretched to the odd number every runner now knows by heart.

Runners, where was the FIRST marathon race actually run? 🏃
Three countries on screen, and three seconds on the clock. The winner of that first race was a water carrier, and the distance we run today was set years later for a royal family's convenience, which is the kind of fact I can't keep to myself.
